title: MIT News
description: Official MIT News: research, campus, and latest articles.

items.title: Fostering community amid Kendall Square’s innovation
items.text: The 18th annual Kendall Square Association Annual Meeting explored how new technologies could be a force for shared prosperity in society.

items.title: Suzy Nelson transformed student life at MIT
items.text: Over the last decade, the vice chancellor has refocused the Institute’s approach to student life to center on student well-being.

items.title: MIT student leaders: Q&A with Association of Student Activities president Hana Sousa
items.text: The senior in chemical engineering volunteers with the ASA as a way to advocate for students and to strengthen bridges between MIT and its student clubs and groups.

items.title: State of Supply Chain Sustainability Report finds corporate commitment at record high, but governance lags behind
items.text: MIT's Center for Transportation and Logistics finds sustainability commitments are strong, but governance gaps and external disruptions prevent execution.

items.title: AI model decodes the language cells use to communicate
items.text: A new computational approach reveals how cells communicate to assemble into tissues. This could accelerate stem cell engineering, improve disease models, and inform therapies.

items.title: Satellite data reveal how Antarctica’s ice cliffs behave over time
items.text: The cliffs don’t always collapse in the runaway process that scientists had expected.

items.title: Building trust in governments through digital platforms
items.text: Governments and private companies often work together to provide public services online. A new study asks: How do these partnerships affect people’s trust in government?

items.title: Q&A: The “collision” between AI, your brain, and society
items.text: In a new book, Professor Eric So explores how the technology affects our thinking skills.

items.title: MIT remembers Thomas Rose, a brilliant researcher and generous colleague
items.text: Faculty, students, staff, family, and friends gathered to remember the assistant professor and archaeometallurgist who died last month.

items.title: Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
items.text: A new machine-learning approach broke records for weather forecasting for an important time frame in emergency planning.

items.title: Hiroshi Ishii honored for contributions to global design and human-computer interaction
items.text: MIT Media Lab professor received the IDSA Special Achievement Award for three decades of research integrating physical and digital environments.

items.title: How artificial neural networks build their own learning machinery
items.text: Machine-learning networks can learn without detailed instructions from a designer. Those that do may offer insight into how the brain reorganizes itself during learning.

items.title: MIT Lincoln Laboratory hosts National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology
items.text: Roadshow event highlights Massachusetts' defense-biotechnology ecosystem.

items.title: MIT Farm is growing
items.text: Co-founders Aleks Banaś and Zachary Rapaport see architecture and farming as deeply complementary disciplines. Their nascent club is having a sizeable impact at the Institute.

items.title: Reprogrammed NK immune cells target cancer and autoimmune disorders
items.text: A new approach can program these cells inside the body and shows promise against diseases caused by dysfunctional T cells, including lymphoma and autoimmune hepatitis.

items.title: Q&A: Building accountability behind our words — and AI’s — in civic conversations
items.text: Professor Deb Roy contends there should be someone who is “answerable” for every piece of text in public life, no matter its origins.

items.title: Exploring how plants thrive in a changing environment
items.text: Associate Professor David Des Marais studies how plants interact with their surroundings and adapt over time.

items.title: Economists Robert Hall PhD ’67 and Michael Woodford PhD ’83 share Nobel Prize
items.text: The MIT alumni are honored for work that illuminates how government policy can spur growth in response to economic downturns.

items.title: 3 Questions: What is the best path forward for AI in academia?
items.text: MIT Statistics and Data Science Center Director Alexander (Sasha) Rakhlin shares important considerations for departments and institutions.

items.title: Supporting systems of success
items.text: In the MIT class 6.C31 (Hack Yourself) students apply computer science strategies to personal growth goals.

items.title: Shape-sensing sheet digitally tracks its movement as it bends and twists
items.text: Developed by MIT engineers, this flexible material could be used as a wearable, motion-monitoring “skin” in physical therapy, virtual reality, and gaming.

items.title: Using AI to mitigate the growing environmental threat of data centers
items.text: By rethinking how large cloud computing systems operate, Associate Professor Christina Delimitrou seeks to make data centers more energy efficient.

items.title: Margaret Hamilton, computing pioneer who led software development for the Apollo program, dies at 90
items.text: Over two decades at MIT, Hamilton forged new paths in computer science and engineering. Her groundbreaking work included leading the team that programmed the first computers that took humans to the moon.

items.title: Discovering the value of humanistic inquiry
items.text: Students in MIT’s Concourse program delve deeply into the human condition, debate challenging questions, and learn to develop judgment about issues that can’t be quantified.

items.title: Turning the tide on Massachusetts shellfishing data
items.text: MIT researchers built a cloud-based platform to help Massachusetts coastal towns and the state manage shellfishing closures, giving thousands of permit holders a clearer view of where they can fish.

items.title: Planning system ensures a robot’s flight path will remain collision-free
items.text: This new method, called “SANDO,” could help disaster-response robots navigate dangerous, unknown environments.

items.title: Supercomputing researchers document evolution of AI hardware
items.text: An ongoing survey tracks the latest AI accelerator systems to keep hardware relevant for Lincoln Laboratory staff and sponsors.

items.title: Chris Bourg named vice provost and Barbara K. Ostrom (1978) Director of the MIT Libraries
items.text: As director, Bourg has focused on digital access, open and equitable scholarly publishing, and expanded support for data-intensive research.

items.title: MIT announces the MIT for America initiative, to strengthen STEM education across the country
items.text: The effort aims to help U.S. learners from kindergarten to community college, with an emphasis on math, making, and the constructive use of AI.

items.title: Astronomers catch a star slowly snacking on a brown dwarf, 300 light years away
items.text: The discovery reveals a new way that stars and planetary companions can interact.

items.title: MIT releases financials and endowment figures for 2026
items.text: The Institute’s pooled investments returned 10.3 percent last year; endowment stands at $29.2 billion.

items.title: Met Warehouse dedication ceremony launches new era
items.text: Once a storage castle, now a design stronghold, the landmark building is a major new hub at MIT.

items.title: Computational tools for society’s most complex challenges
items.text: Associate Professor Cathy Wu uses reinforcement learning to help map out improvements to transportation and other multifaceted systems.

items.title: Documenting the tech worker movement
items.text: Writing as a participant and researcher, PhD student JS Tan SM ’22 has co-authored a new book about the rise of tech worker protests and the employer backlash that followed.

items.title: The next generation’s guide to the new space economy
items.text: An industry report published by students in an MIT aerospace entrepreneurship class lays out guidance for aspiring space leaders and investors.

items.title: 3 Questions: A new resource to empower young entrepreneurs
items.text: Martin Trust Center Managing Director Bill Aulet introduces Dear Dreamer, a free platform for middle and high school students who want to learn about entrepreneurship.

items.title: MIT class project turns into an FDA-cleared treatment for tremors
items.text: Wristband device from Encora Therapeutics started as a project in 2.009, MIT’s iconic product-design class.

items.title: New tool lets users repair AI-generated 3D models, then fabricate them just the way they want
items.text: “InstructMesh” can generate designs for everyday objects that are easy to edit and fabricate for both experts and newcomers to 3D modeling.

items.title: Governor Healey and President Kornbluth launch MIT Future Fest
items.text: The new, five-day MIT event reaches takeoff with a forum about discovery and innovation.

items.title: Craig Rowe soars to new heights
items.text: The aircraft mechanic is the lead crew chief of Lincoln Laboratory’s Gulfstream IV and recently oversaw the plane’s major modification.

items.title: MIT Transit Lab to develop an AI platform for public transit agencies
items.text: With $2.1 million funding from Google.org, the open-source Public Transit Intelligence Hub will unify public transit monitoring, operations, and passenger communication.

items.title: This game-playing AI is the new champ at Stratego
items.text: Able to defeat top-ranked human players and more efficient than other models, the new system could help decision-makers in military maneuvers or business negotiations.

items.title: Lung cancers can use two different mechanisms to evade KRAS-inhibiting drugs
items.text: Some tumor cells develop resistance by amplifying the KRAS gene, while others change their tumor type, MIT researchers have found.

items.title: Climate Action Learning Lab bridges research and policy for effective climate solutions
items.text: J-PAL North America’s Learning Lab supported a second cohort of U.S. government and nonprofit organizations in building and using rigorous evidence to advance effective decarbonization and adaptation strategies.

items.title: Powered by muscle cells, a paper-thin robot swims through watery maze
items.text: MIT engineers’ new aquabot offers a way to design small, efficient “biohybrid” robots.

items.title: The effects of an “algorithmic monoculture” depend on the details
items.text: In a study focusing on hiring decisions, MIT researchers found the use of a single algorithm by many firms could benefit job seekers in certain situations.

items.title: Who we become when we talk to machines
items.text: Professor Sherry Turkle’s new book, “Artificial Intimacy,” offers a withering critique of chatbots and the antisocial dynamics she believes they encourage.

items.title: Pressurized experiments could help wind farms generate more power
items.text: A new way of simulating wind turbines in the field shows how tweaking turbine operation could unlock tens of thousands of dollars per turbine every year.

items.title: New formulation helps RNA vaccines withstand high temperatures
items.text: MIT engineers have found a way to stabilize the lipid nanoparticles used to deliver RNA vaccines, which could allow the vaccines to be more widely distributed.

items.title: MIT students gain a humanist lens on technical innovation in Tulsa, Oklahoma
items.text: The PKG Center for Social Impact expands Code.Tulsa experiential learning program.

items.title: A new technique could accelerate the development of RNA therapies
items.text: MIT chemical engineers found a way to rapidly produce lipid nanoparticles of varying sizes, which could make it easier to develop new vaccines and therapeutics.

items.title: Scattering neutrinos to probe the fundamental laws of the universe
items.text: As she became integral to an international particle physics experiment, PhD student Faith Reyes found confidence in herself as a scientist.

items.title: Estimating suicide risk from text
items.text: A new language-processing tool could help identify the highest-risk individuals from natural language, enabling swifter interventions.

items.title: Biologists identify a cellular pathway that allows colorectal cancer to metastasize
items.text: They also found that obesity may put patients at higher risk for activation of the pathway. Drugs that block the pathway may help prevent metastasis.

items.title: New cell-collection device could improve early cancer detection
items.text: MIT researchers developed a handheld system that gently collects living cells from patient samples to aid cancer testing and development of personalized medicines.

items.title: The promise and peril of using visual AI to study cities
items.text: In their new book, “How AI Sees the City,” the leaders of MIT’s Senseable City Lab examine the technology’s implications for researching urban life.

items.title: MIT welcomes David Siegel SM ’86, PhD ’91 as its next Innovation Fellow
items.text: Computer scientist, entrepreneur, and philanthropist will collaborate with the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing to advance AI and scientific discovery.

items.title: FUNdaMENTALs of precision design
items.text: Precision, repeatability, and fun are the focus in mechanical engineering course 2.70 (Fundamentals of Precision Product Design).

items.title: Featured video: Behind the lens at Lincoln Laboratory
items.text: Staff photographer Niki Fandel captures the people and technology advancing Lincoln Laboratory’s national security mission.

items.title: How the brain keeps its options straight at decision time
items.text: Making a decision requires juggling a set of options without getting them confused or losing track of them. A new MIT study shows how neurons encode information to maximize clarity throughout the process.

items.title: Poitras Center to fuel early careers of 50 young scientists dedicated to psychiatric disorders research
items.text: Patricia and James Poitras ’63 provide fellowships for graduate students and postdocs who will shape the future of mental health research.

items.title: MIT named the nation’s top university by U.S. News for 2026-27
items.text: The Institute’s undergraduate engineering, computer science, and economics programs are No. 1; its business program is No. 2.

items.title: Podcast: SHASS’s special sauce
items.text: Established after World War II, the School of the Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences is an integral part of the MIT experience. Three faculty reflect on the school’s ongoing impact.

items.title: Finding purpose through research
items.text: This summer, BSG-MSRP-Bio student Marina Milea investigated how lung cancers become resistant to targeted therapies, gaining hands-on research experience in the Jacks Lab at the Koch Institute.

items.title: A home a world away from home
items.text: One graduate student family treasures the community they found alongside other MIT student parents.

items.title: Carter Stubbs named Institute auditor
items.text: New Audit Division leader brings track record of collaboration, deep knowledge of audit program and MIT operations to role.

items.title: Batteries that safely break down in the GI tract could improve ingestible devices
items.text: Made from “bioresorbable” materials, the new batteries could power capsules for drug delivery, sensing, and other applications.

items.title: Unmasking “zombie cells” in aging tissue with an AI-powered barcode
items.text: Tracking down senescent cells, which accumulate as we age, could help diagnose age-related disorders and guide researchers working on new treatments.

items.title: MIT researchers are mapping extreme weather risks — and building tools to act on them
items.text: The Climate Grand Challenges “New World of Weather” project shows how modeling, planning tools, and infrastructure analysis are translating research into real-world resilience.

items.title: A new chapter for MIT Reads
items.text: A new focus on fiction and memoir aims to help the MIT community celebrate the power of storytelling and strengthen social connection.

items.title: A new understanding of how enzymes influence bacterial protein production
items.text: Novel research expands scientific understanding of how RNA shapes the reading of genetic information.

items.title: Fueling a return journey from Mars
items.text: PhD candidate Lanie McKinney is building technology to convert the Red Planet’s atmosphere into propellant for bringing astronauts home.

items.title: Meet the 2026 tenured professors in the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences
items.text: Faculty members granted tenure in Comparative Media Studies/Writing, Economics, Political Science, and Theater.

items.title: MIT School of Engineering faculty and staff receive awards in spring 2026
items.text: Faculty members and researchers were honored in recognition of their scholarship, service, and overall excellence.

items.title: Understanding the world, from the Cold War to the age of AI
items.text: For 75 years, the Center for International Studies has brought together social scientists, engineers, and practitioners to understand global change, shape public debate, and address generational challenges.

items.title: Lincoln Laboratory summer research interns take on national security challenges
items.text: Anna Raymaker and Vivek Jagadeesh tackled cybersecurity threats to ships and inside operating systems, respectively.

items.title: Robotic lab sets up and runs optics experiments on demand
items.text: The autonomous system could speed up testing of high-tech materials for applications such as solar cells, sensors, video displays, and quantum technologies.

items.title: Faces of MIT: Jay Wilcoxson
items.text: Combining a background in private law practice with a passion for problem-solving, Wilcoxson supports MIT’s mission and principles through his work as counsel.

items.title: “Technology is the equalizer”
items.text: Using knowledge gained from MIT’s free learning materials, an educator in rural India builds apps to reach students who can’t make it to school.

items.title: New artist residency program at MIT expands views of the cosmos
items.text: Inaugural artist Amy Karle will join astrophysicists at MIT’s Kavli Institute to explore questions about the universe and translate them into an immersive multimedia experience.

items.title: Nanoscale mechanics could enable brain-inspired computing
items.text: A new device uses reconfigurable motion to mimic the firing behavior of a neuron, which could lead to more efficient computing.

items.title: New AI technique could make minimally invasive surgeries safer and more precise
items.text: This patient-specific method, called xvr, helps doctors use X-rays for surgical navigation in fields such as orthopedics and neurosurgery.

items.title: MIT startups inspire with impressive presentations at Demo Day 2026
items.text: The event featured ventures solving problems in manufacturing, cybersecurity, health care spending, and more.

items.title: Measure by measure, studying society accurately
items.text: Naoki Egami has become a standout in political methodology, helping refine tools that give scholars durable results.

items.title: How MIT student communities help develop lifelong skills and connections
items.text: Members of the Institute’s fraternities, sororities, and independent living groups translate their MIT experiences into cherished memories, friendships, and lessons about leadership and service.

items.title: MIT makes progress on campus climate goals
items.text: Innovative strategies, technologies, and collaborations are helping MIT advance solutions on campus and beyond.

items.title: 3 Questions: Putting nuclear waste into perspective
items.text: Professor Haruko Wainwright believes the risks posed by radioactive wastes cannot be properly assessed without also considering the hazards of chemical wastes.

items.title: Marine bacteria team up to break down one of the ocean's toughest carbon-storing molecules
items.text: Researchers reveal how communities of marine bacteria divide the task of degrading fucoidan, a key player in ocean carbon storage.

items.title: New method enables AI for safety-critical situations
items.text: The “HardFlow” algorithm could help generative AI models produce high-quality outputs that obey strict requirements when “pretty close” doesn’t cut it.

items.title: MIT spinout turns plastic waste into resilient building materials
items.text: Atlas Building Composites is commercializing MIT research to turn plastic waste into parts for buildings and other infrastructure.

items.title: Lifesaving Lincoln Laboratory device wins 2026 Excellence in Technology Transfer Award
items.text: The handheld catheterization device AI-GUIDE, created by Lincoln Laboratory and Massachusetts General Hospital,  promises improved health outcomes for injured service members and civilians.

items.title: MIT Schwarzman College of Computing launches pilot to help educators teach AI across disciplines
items.text: A weeklong summer workshop brought higher education faculty to campus to explore how AI and machine learning materials can be adapted for their classrooms.

items.title: Injectable nanodevices could provide effective treatment for drug-resistant glioblastoma
items.text: MIT researchers show implanted nanoantennas can be activated wirelessly to kill brain cancer cells without damage to healthy tissue.

items.title: A burst of “pink noise” may lead to more restorative sleep
items.text: Delivered at just the right time, this type of auditory stimulus can strengthen the flow of cerebrospinal fluid, which clears debris from the brain and keeps it healthy.

items.title: An electrochemical approach turns ammonia into pure hydrogen
items.text: An MIT team has demonstrated a more efficient way to extract pure hydrogen gas from hydrogen carrier molecules.

items.title: Study predicts large disparities in access to food, water, and energy in 2050
items.text: In some regions of the world, the poorest people may spend about 50 percent of their income on food, while the richest spend about 5 percent.

items.title: Researchers tune into Arctic under-ice sounds and test through-ice communication
items.text: The work is part of a multiyear effort to develop a distributed sensor network for relaying data collected from this critical region.

items.title: New method allows scientists to follow gene activity over time in the same cells
items.text: In the new method, cells package and export their RNA, enabling researchers to sequence and analyze the RNA without killing the cells.

items.title: Stories from the steel mills: A model for sharing workers’ histories
items.text: MIT anthropologist Chris Walley developed a project for people in Southeast Chicago to tell their histories — an approach any community can adopt.

items.title: How architects turned a hulking brick box into MIT’s newest academic hub
items.text: A venerable storage facility has become a 21st-century architectural tour de force. Here are the key decisions that transformed the Met Warehouse.

items.title: Governor Healey, MIT President Kornbluth to Kick Off Festivities at MIT Future Fest
items.text: The five-day festival will explore the future of science, technology, art and design from Wednesday, Sept. 30 to Sunday, Oct. 4

items.title: Faculty receive promotions in the School of Architecture and Planning for 2026
items.text: The range of faculty disciplines showcases the breadth of research and scholarship across the school.

items.title: 3 Questions: The essential role of international engagement
items.text: Duane Boning, MIT’s vice provost for international activities, discusses the Institute’s approach to global engagement.

items.title: Associate Professor Thomas Rose, an expert in archaeometallurgy, dies at 37
items.text: Colleagues remember Rose as an enthusiastic and gracious friend who had recently started a promising research track at MIT.

items.title: Fabrication platform could enable flexible, transparent next-generation photonic chips
items.text: This scalable process produces high-performance chips for applications like discreet wearables or pliable augmented-reality displays.

items.title: New qubit architecture enables faster, more accurate operations
items.text: This advance could be a big step toward developing a scalable, practical quantum computer.

items.title: Giving farmers a more sustainable way to protect crops
items.text: Led by Andee Wallace PhD ’20, Robigo uses cutting-edge biotechnology to engineer microbes to fight pests, reducing the need for harmful chemical pesticides.

items.title: Building foundations that last
items.text: Assistant Professor Iwnetim Abate creates space for ambitious research and sustainable growth for his graduate students.

items.title: From MIT to IBM, expediting AI and quantum deployment
items.text: MIT affiliates engage with the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab to bring rigorous theory to production systems.

items.title: System helps humans predict when self-driving cars will make mistakes
items.text: A new method, called CW-Net, translates the reasoning process of an autonomous vehicle’s AI system into understandable concepts that explain its behavior.

items.title: New research shows a neutrino laser is impossible
items.text: Due to physical and fundamental limitations, an earlier proposal for producing laserlike beams of neutrinos cannot be achieved, scientists report.

items.title: Walter Torous named executive director of MIT Center for Real Estate
items.text: The senior lecturer, already director of the degree program, will now oversee all aspects of the center’s activities and operations.

items.title: Cognition and consciousness arise from analog computations, says new theory
items.text: The brain's ability to generate quick, nimble volitional thought — and a unified awareness of thought and experience — arises from analog computations, MIT neuroscientists argue in a new review.

items.title: Atlas of the brain’s striatum could guide researchers to new drug treatments
items.text: A new study reveals insights into populations of neurons affected by Huntington’s disease, schizophrenia, addiction, and other disorders.

items.title: Ila Kumar: Innovating with communities
items.text: The PhD student works to give young people an active role in shaping digital technologies that can support their own well-being.

items.title: “You're going to see the impact in 10 years” - President Kornbluth returns to GBH’s “Boston Public Radio” to discuss scientific funding and curiosity driven research
items.text: Kornbluth weighed in on the consequences of cuts to federal funding for science and the value of curiosity driven research.

items.title: Translating economic growth into better lives
items.text: Graduate student Lyonel Tanganco investigates how to improve public policy interventions and address challenges in nutrition, climate, and development.

items.title: Gulfstream IV makes its long-awaited return to Lincoln Laboratory
items.text: The modified aircraft will support an ongoing US Air Force program to assess and enhance the survivability of air and space vehicles.

items.title: MIT Quantum Initiative launches postdoctoral fellowship program
items.text: The Institute welcomes its first cohort of QMIT Fellows this fall to advance interdisciplinary quantum research.

items.title: At MIT convocation, a warm welcome for the Class of 2030
items.text: The Institute is “so glad and so grateful” to have this year’s new undergraduates aboard, President Kornbluth said at the annual greeting ceremony.

items.title: Study: Peptides can form well-defined structures in harsh, Venus-like conditions
items.text: New research offers support for the possibility that complex biological molecules could exist in the highly acidic environment of Venus’s cloud layer.

items.title: Playing against climate risk
items.text: Climate scientist Sai Ravela is using games to help coastal communities find creative adaptations to climate change.

items.title: How an MIT research project became a global programming language
items.text: With millions of users across the world, Julia has been used to conduct cutting-edge research and to design new drugs, jet engines, heat pumps, and more.

items.title: How an MIT graduate student helped a team of young scientists test their experiment at CERN
items.text: Physics PhD student Manu Srivastava helped high school students in India develop a test that could contribute to one of the world’s largest neutrino experiments.

items.title: How MIT Sandbox has turned student ideas into $8.7 billion in global impact
items.text: Through a decade of non-dilutive funding, hands-on mentorship, and a safe space to fail fast, the MIT Sandbox Innovation Fund Program has helped students translate curiosity into real-world impact.

items.title: Gage Coon: An Earth scientist exploring the power of microbes
items.text: The PhD student’s research on how microorganisms digest compounds in their environment could enable advances in wastewater treatment.

items.title: Looking beyond natural sequences
items.text: A new machine-learning framework aims to improve the success rate of computational protein design while moving away from results that reproduce sequences found in nature.

items.title: New type of attack can slip past the defenses in your computer’s processor
items.text: MIT CSAIL researchers found a way to exploit a split-second gap in chip security — and used it to acquire a Linux system’s password file.

items.title: MIT engineers create a system for building shape-changing smart devices
items.text: Dubbed “bifur-circuits,” these interactive building blocks could be used to develop reconfigurable robotic grippers or customized assistive devices.

items.title: MIT student leaders: Q&A with McCormick Hall co-president Sydney Baller
items.text: The rising senior loves her dorm and its community and wants to serve as a bridge to its next residents as the building heads into renovations.

items.title: AI helps design new materials that work in the real world
items.text: The “CrysVCD” tool developed at MIT could cut the huge amounts of time and money spent on screening out chemically unstable designs.

items.title: Retooling to help democracy revive
items.text: Deindustrialization didn’t only hurt some workers, Daron Acemoglu says in a new book; it shrank the coalition supporting democracy, which needs expanding.

items.title: Cells use a little-known molecule to protect themselves from iron overload
items.text: This discovery points toward new combination strategies against cancer, and may explain the iron buildup seen in disorders such as early-onset Parkinson’s disease.

items.title: A new kind of aircraft departs an MIT classroom and arrives at an Ohio factory
items.text: Electra’s hybrid, fixed-wing aircraft, which grew out of a class project, could make travel easier for passengers taking shorter trips.

items.title: The secret love life of the longfin squid
items.text: MIT Sea Grant resident artist and acclaimed underwater photographer Keith Ellenbogen captures an intimate look at courtship and communication in a hidden spawning spectacle off Cape Cod.

items.title: Brain circuit keeps tabs on what just happened to aid judgment of what’s happening now
items.text: To keep track of what’s going on in front of it, the brain relies not only on what it sees, but also a comparison with what it just saw. A new study pinpoints the circuit that provides that service.

items.title: Meteorite dust holds records of magnetism that may have helped form the sun
items.text: The discovery likely represents the earliest known evidence of a magnetic field in the infant solar system.

items.title: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data
items.text: A new algorithm learns to anticipate the unprecedented scenarios that critical infrastructure and global supply chains are least prepared for.

items.title: Language skills stay strong in older adults, even while other cognitive abilities decline
items.text: MIT researchers find that activity in the brain’s language network is nearly identical in young and old people.

items.title: The importance of indoor airflow patterns in spreading airborne disease
items.text: Researchers explore how a key factor can mitigate or promote tuberculosis transmission.

items.title: Paving the way for greener ammonia production
items.text: New MIT research could lead to better materials for a fossil-fuel-free process for making the chemical that's essential to fertilizer and other products.

items.title: MIT engineers design a better controller for operating construction diggers
items.text: The new, more intuitive system could speed up the training process for excavator operators.

items.title: The game’s the thing
items.text: MIT senior Kayode Dada has a passion for designing games, and a penchant for building community.

items.title: How the Toxoplasma parasite adapts to crowded conditions in host cells
items.text: A new study by Whitehead Institute researchers identifies how the widespread parasite Toxoplasma gondii survives in crowded environments in infected cells, which helps it persist in long-lasting brain cysts.

items.title: Creating innovations that scale across borders
items.text: A new book coauthored by Professor Amos Winter asserts that, to solve major challenges and deliver products of value to consumers in both developed and emerging markets, innovators must think and act globally.

items.title: Flipping the script on biology education, and scaling it up
items.text: Using a modular kit, the MIT Edgerton Center is bringing a hands-on biology curriculum to Massachusetts’ second-largest school district.

items.title: Securing wireless communication in next-generation devices
items.text: A new, scalable technique could enable powerful radars and sensors based on quantum technology that works at room temperature.

items.title: Cell-preservation technique could make CAR-T cell therapy more accessible
items.text: MIT researchers’ approach, which uses naturally occurring sugars as antifreeze, could make it easier for hospitals to deploy this type of cancer treatment.

items.title: Startup brings ancient Roman concrete technology to modern construction
items.text: Dmat is commercializing findings from the lab of Associate Professor Admir Masic to make concrete longer-lasting and more sustainable.

items.title: When AI art has no author: Study finds generated images often can’t be traced to training data
items.text: A new method for surgically removing training examples from a model reveals that as datasets grow, the link between what a model learns and what it produces dissolves.

items.title: Anthea Coster awarded International Union of Radio Science Appleton Prize
items.text: The MIT Haystack Observatory principal research scientist is honored for lifetime contributions to ionospheric research.

items.title: How 35 percent of US employees are left on the margins
items.text: In a new book, Paul Osterman details his research finding more than one-third of the country’s workers are “disposable,” with little security or chance of job advancement.

items.title: Tackling rare genetic disorders with patient-focused science
items.text: Shannon Knight, a brain and cognitive sciences PhD candidate and McGovern Institute researcher, focuses on developing a novel gene therapy.

items.title: DNA shaper steers nervous system development
items.text: A study of worms finds a protein that helps shape the structure of the genome is critical for establishing the identity of some neurons.

items.title: Q&A: Rethinking how innovation happens
items.text: In his latest book, Professor Eugene Fitzgerald examines the forces that turn breakthroughs into value — and why innovation resists simple formulas.

items.title: Mathematical framework connects biological principles to manufacturable, adaptive materials
items.text: The new framework could streamline the design process of robotic grippers or aerospace components that exhibit complex behaviors found in nature.

items.title: MIT engineers connect bacteria to create living transistors
items.text: By wiring together colonies of these bacteria, the researchers built circuits that can perform complicated calculations.

items.title: Flexible brain circuits can switch between different tasks
items.text: Neuroscientists have discovered circuits in the prefrontal cortex that can be repurposed to store different types of information.

items.title: Professor Emeritus Chiang Chung Mei, pioneering scholar of ocean wave dynamics and fluid mechanics, dies at 91
items.text: A towering figure in theoretical hydrodynamics is remembered for his intellectual rigor, generosity, and lifelong devotion to his students.

items.title: Drug that targets an inflammatory enzyme could help prevent lung cancer
items.text: A new study by MIT researchers shows that inhibiting caspase-1 can reduce the risk of tumor growth.

items.title: Cells pulse together as they grow — and malignant cells pulse the longest
items.text: MIT researchers discovered a cellular dance that may offer clues to the development of cancer, asthma, and other diseases.

items.title: High-speed microscopy reveals electrical activity across the brain
items.text: The new technique could help scientists learn how the entire brain works to generate decisions and emotions.

items.title: Researchers uncover hidden pore network within nuclear fuel
items.text: New understanding of how nuclear fuel breaks down and changes in an operating nuclear reactor could help keep some reactors running longer, will inform the next generation of nuclear reactor fuel systems.

items.title: Featured video: An “MIT story” about an iconic professor
items.text: A new short film from MIT Open Learning explores the influential career of Institute Professor and School of Engineering Dean Paula Hammond.

items.title: MIT selected to lead new NSF materials research center
items.text: The Materials Research Science and Engineering Center unites researchers across disciplines to develop technologies for medical imaging, sustainable metals production, and next-generation electronics.

items.title: Astronomers discover a brand-new type of astrophysical object: A black hole star
items.text: The mashup of a black hole and an enormous star has never been seen before and could explain the mysterious little red dots often found in deep-space images.

items.title: Met Warehouse opens as the new home of MIT’s School of Architecture and Planning
items.text: In a feat of adaptive reuse, a massive, century-old brick storage facility has been turned into a contemporary hub for collaboration and creative work.

items.title: How to design a space habitat that supports its residents’ mental health
items.text: A new online platform helps engineers look beyond survival mode when designing habitats for extreme living conditions.

items.title: 3 Questions: MIT Sloan launches Evening MBA
items.text: Dean Richard Locke discusses a new program that expands access for working professionals while deepening connections to Greater Boston’s innovation economy.

items.title: The mystery of the Chinese tea chest label
items.text: MIT historian Tristan Brown uncovers the true origins of an artifact once thought to be a relic of the Boston Tea Party.

items.title: On the hunt for dark matter
items.text: From Broadway to MIT’s Laboratory for Nuclear Science, PhD student Jessica Fry doesn’t do anything halfway. Now she’s hunting for the universe’s most elusive particle.

items.title: With a feel for physics, AI models simulate a wider range of real-world scenarios
items.text: “GeoPT” helps AI models understand the basics of physics so they can simulate how objects respond to things like wind and water more efficiently and accurately.

items.title: High-orbit satellites could light the way for travel to the moon
items.text: Acting as cooperative optical beacons, the satellites could provide GPS-like navigation and communications support for spacecraft operating across cislunar space.

items.title: MIT researchers tackle the economic realities of fusion power
items.text: Their new study aims to give budding industry a framework for understanding how fusion can be profitable.

items.title: Physicists watch a material’s electrons assemble, and reassemble, into coexisting phases
items.text: The study could help scientists understand how superconductivity and other more complex phenomena emerge in quantum materials.

items.title: Akirah Bradley-Armstrong named vice chancellor for student life
items.text: An experienced student affairs leader is joining MIT to oversee the next chapter for the Division of Student Life.

items.title: A new way to watch heat move through electronics
items.text: MIT researchers can now precisely measure how heat moves through multilayered materials like computer chips.

items.title: Then and now: How MIT Lincoln Laboratory has served as a driving force in national security innovation
items.text: Members of the laboratory community reflect on technology impacts that shaped the United States and the world over the past 75 years.

items.title: Researchers make air-stable, ultrathin superconductors, for more scalable quantum devices
items.text: A new technique produces wafer-scale samples, overcoming a major roadblock to using these materials in quantum technologies.

items.title: Scientists unveil more than 600 new tissue models of human cancer
items.text: Derived from patient tumor samples and available to researchers around the world, the cells will aid the development of new cancer treatments.

items.title: Past is prologue for geopolitical developments
items.text: DUSP Associate Professor Jason Jackson’s latest book compares how two countries chose radically different paths to economic independence.

items.title: Reframing leadership as a design problem
items.text: Nicholas de Monchaux reflects on guiding the MIT Department of Architecture through a period of dramatic change for the profession.

items.title: Alexander Rakhlin named director of  the MIT Statistics and Data Science Center
items.text: An expert in machine learning, statistics, and computation, Rakhlin succeeds Professor Ankur Moitra.

items.title: Connecting students with the future of microelectronics
items.text: The 2026 NEMC Hub-sponsored externship gave students access to world-class research, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, and professionals driving innovation across the Northeast.

items.title: Using reason, again and again
items.text: Philosopher Brian Hedden studies decision-making over time — and recently chose to return to alma mater MIT, where he is now connecting ethics and computing.

items.title: Building energy security through more sustainable batteries
items.text: PhD student Hugh Smith works to develop sodium-ion batteries, whose components are more abundant and accessible than those of conventional lithium-ion technology.

items.title: Daniela Rus receives Bavarian Minister-President's High-Tech Prize
items.text: Director of CSAIL and MIT professor honored for her contributions to robotics, artificial intelligence, and autonomous systems.

items.title: Connecting research to policy on Capitol Hill
items.text: MIT students and postdocs discussed science funding and research with policymakers in Washington during the MIT Science Policy Initiative’s annual Congressional Visit Days.

items.title: How a medical database developed at MIT evolved into a global standard of data-sharing
items.text: The visionary PhysioNet platform launched 25 years ago, based on a system developed at MIT in the 1970s. It has become one of the most comprehensive biomedical and clinical data repositories in existence.

items.title: Professor Emeritus Robert Cohen, pioneering polymers researcher and devoted mentor, dies at 79
items.text: Architect of MIT’s interdisciplinary Program in Polymers and Soft Matter and the PhD in chemical engineering practice is remembered for his passion for mentorship and education.

items.title: Making robots faster by helping them think ahead
items.text: By planning actions based on the future position of a robot, the VLASH technique streamlines motions and accelerates performance.

items.title: Emery Brown, Daniel Hastings, and Douglas Lauffenburger named Institute Professors
items.text: Longtime professors and experts in the fields of anesthesiology, aerospace engineering, and biological engineering, respectively, receive MIT’s highest faculty honor.

items.title: Diana Grass: Listening to the body’s language
items.text: The PhD candidate builds soft bioelectronic technologies to decode signals between the brain and the rest of the body.

items.title: MIT Professor Susumu Tonegawa, renowned molecular biologist and Nobel laureate, dies at 86
items.text: Tonegawa made landmark discoveries about how the immune system generates antibody diversity and how the brain forms memories.

items.title: Bringing the data to every sideline
items.text: PhD candidate Henry Wang works with FIFA and other organizations to advance the way sports are played, analyzed, and refereed.

items.title: MIT-Kalaniyot program expands, with new cohort of scholars
items.text: The innovative effort bringing researchers from Israel to campus keeps growing while enhancing community connections and academic inquiry.

items.title: Q&A: What is agentic AI today, and what do we want it to be?
items.text: Computer scientist Phillip Isola cuts through the hype to explain how AI agents work and what the future might hold for this rapidly advancing technology.
